concerns.text: The plan mandates a mandatory permutation test (10 000 shuffles) on the set of scalar upper‑limit values (see “mandatory permutation test (10 000 shuffles) to assess robustness per Constitution Principle VII”). Permuting study labels does not change the statistic of interest (the minimum 90 % CL limit per nucleus), making the test tautological: every permutation yields the identical combined bound, so the empirical p‑value is either 0 or 1 by definition. This violates Principle VII, which is intended for raw, vector‑valued data where label shuffling alters the test statistic. The validation is therefore circular and provides no information about robustness.

Applying a permutation test to a scalar aggregate (minimum limit) is a category error. Permutation testing is appropriate when the null hypothesis concerns the relationship between two variables (e.g., polarization vs. momentum). Here the analysis only uses published scalar upper limits, so the permutation test cannot assess significance or robustness. The plan should either (a) drop the permutation test or (b) replace it with a method that genuinely probes variability, such as a sensitivity analysis based on confidence‑level uncertainties or a Bayesian hierarchical model.
